Biometric Quality vs Failure

Fingerprint quality falls with age and with manual work (worn ridges, cuts, calluses), and with dust, heat or wet hands. This page shows how strongly capture quality decides whether a genuine person gets through.

Reset Showing all data

Failure rate by biometric quality band

What this shows: genuine attempts with quality 20-40 fail 73.8% of the time, against 6.0% at quality 60-80. Biometric failures (orange) dominate at low quality; system failures (slate) stay roughly flat because the network and device do not care about your fingerprint.

Fingerprint vs iris (genuine users)

What this shows: Fingerprint: FRR 24.7%, mean quality 55.9, 5,746 visits; Iris: FRR 3.5%, mean quality 84.8, 138 visits. Iris is far less affected by age and manual work, but in this data it is only available on high-quality devices, so it is rarely offered to the people who need it most.

Biometric quality vs match score

What this shows: each dot is one attempt that reached the matching step. Genuine users (teal circles) rise with quality; below the dashed line (0.60) they are rejected even though they are who they say they are. Impostors (orange triangles) stay low regardless of quality. Attempts that failed on network or device have no score and are not shown.
